UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT
FOR THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF VIRGINIA
ALEXANDRIA DIVISION
MARVELLE J. BALLENTINE,
Plaintiff,
Case No. 1:26-cv-02331
V.
KATIE HALL, individually;
NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED
CHILDREN;
META PLATFORMS, INC.;
and JOHN/JANE DOES 1-6,
Defendants.
MEMORANDUM IN SUPPORT OF PLAINTIFF'S MOTION FOR LEAVE TO
SUPPLEMENT ECF NO. 133
INTRODUCTION
Imagine receiving two letters that indicate evidence may exist connecting you with the
lowest form of human life — individuals who commit crimes against children.
Imagine the flashbacks to your own trauma. Imagine the tears shed while hunched over a
toilet bowl.
Imagine the mortal fear of filing another piece of paper in any of your current cases.
Imagine drafting Rule 41 dismissal notices, printing them out, and — with tears flowing — hearing
your wife ask: "Are you just gonna tell your sons you gave up?"
Then imagine the promise you made to your uncle, your "other father," before he passed.
The promise was simple: that you would be the greatest pro se litigant of all time.
1

Then imagine proceeding.
Marvelle J. Ballentine proceeded.
The day after he filed this action, he offered NCMEC a way out. No money. No admission.
Testimony only. He believed it would end the dispute that day. NCMEC did not take it. NCMEC
says the letters are true. Plaintiff says prove it. NCMEC refuses. Plaintiff asks the Court for three
interrogatories. Denied as premature. Plaintiff asks for a Rule 26(f) conference. Denied. Plaintiff
asks for a Rule 16(b) scheduling order. Denied. Plaintiff asks for a settlement conference. NCMEC
answers that it has no interest in settlement and that a conference would cost it money.
So here is an offer that costs one hour. One witness. One oath. Tell him about the letters
and the two reports. He will pay for the recording. When the hour is over, he will dismiss his
claims against NCMEC and Ms. Hall and release every NCMEC employee, whatever the witness
says.
He printed Rule 41 notices once, in tears. He will sign one now, for one hour of sworn
testimony, so that his sons do not have to wonder whether their father's name ever appeared in a
report concerning the sexual exploitation of children.
The answer has been pursued in courts from the East Coast to the West Coast, against
resistance from the defense and from the Courts. That resistance serves no one - least of all
children — if Mr. Ballentine is a predator.
This Court knows what such conduct earns. On September 23, 2026, Judge Alston
sentenced a man to eighteen years in prison for attempted sexual exploitation of a child arising
from communications initiated on Facebook. United States v. Bonilla Canales, No. 1:26-cr-00004-
RDA (E.D. Va. Sept. 23, 2026). The Court sat as factfinder, heard that evidence, and found it
proved. Id., ECF No. 59 at 1, 3-4. Should evidence ever warrant prosecuting Mr. Ballentine for

such conduct, he would stand in this very courtroom to answer for it. Today he stands before the
same Court offering to end his case against NCMEC for one hour of testimony about whether the
reports invoked against his name even identify him.
The pen is in NCMEC's hand. It should say: "Accepted."
THE RECORD
A. On April 22, 2026, NCMEC stated in writing that it "has received two (2)
CyberTipline reports concerning (1) Marvelle J. Ballentine, (2) Jay Ballentine, and/or (3) the
account-level identifier jaychizza@icloud.com between July 1, 2022 and the present." ECF No. 5
977.
B.
Plaintiff has declared that, before April 22, 2026, he never used the name
"Marvelle J. Ballentine" to create, register, identify, maintain, access, or operate any account on
any Meta product or service that he used. ECF No. 31 9 3. He used the name "Jay Ballentine." Id. 1
6.
C.
NCMEC's motion to dismiss asserts that "The Statements are True, and Thus Not
Actionable." ECF No. 11 at 8.
D. NCMEC has stated that Plaintiff "cannot plausibly assert that is the case, because
he does not have access to those reports." ECF No. 11 at 9. On November 10, 2026, NCMEC
stated: "the issue is whether NCMEC received such a report, and Plaintiff cannot plausibly assert
that is untrue." ECF No. 139 at 5.
E.
NCMEC has also stated: "NCMEC is not alleged to have stated that Plaintiff
engaged in reportable conduct, nor does NCMEC take that position." ECF No. 139 at 5.
F.
No Defendant has stated in any filing in this action that a CyberTipline report
contains the name "Marvelle J. Ballentine."
3

G. On July 31, 2026, Plaintiff transmitted to NCMEC and Hall a proposed settlement
agreement. It required no payment and no admission. It required no particular answer. Plaintiff
would bear the deposition recording costs. It provided for acceptance by August 14, 2026. Neither
NCMEC nor Hall accepted it.
H.
On November 2, 2026, Plaintiff moved for referral to an early settlement
conference. ECF No. 133.
I.
On November 9, 2026, NCMEC and Hall opposed. The opposition states:
"NCMEC has no interest in settlement." ECF No. 136 at 2.
• A settlement conference would "cause NCME to incur additional fees and
expenses." Id.
"IT]he proverbial 'ship has sailed' in terms of preserving resources." Id.
• Plaintiff "is seeking in excess of $42,000,000.00." Id.
J. On November 10, 2026, NCMEC and Hall moved to extend their time to respond
to Plaintiff's renewed Rule 56 motion until after an answer is due. ECF Nos. 137, 138. The
memorandum states that NCMEC "should not be forced to incur additional litigation expenses
until this Honorable Court resolves the pending motions to dismiss." ECF No. 138 at 5. It states
that "neither NCMEC nor this Court should be required to expend additional resources." Id. It
states: "No Answer has been filed by any defendant to date." Id. at 2.
II.
LEAVE IS WARRANTED BECAUSE THE OFFER ANSWERS THE
OPPOSITION
Local Civil Rule 7(F)(1) provides that after the reply, "InJo further briefs or written
communications may be filed without first obtaining leave of Court." Plaintiff seeks that leave.
The supplement responds to matter that first appeared in ECF No. 136. ECF No. 133
proposed a conference. ECF No. 136 answered that a conference would cost NCMEC fees and
4

that NCMEC has no interest in settlement. Exhibit A requires no conference and no payment. It
asks for one hour of testimony.
Rule 16(a)(5) identifies "facilitating settlement" as a purpose of pretrial management. Rule
16(c)(2)(1) reaches "settling the case." Rule 16(c)(2)(P) reaches "facilitating in other ways the just,
speedy, and inexpensive disposition of the action." The Offer is within each.
Ill.
NCMEC SAYS THE LETTERS ARE TRUE. THE OFFER ASKS NCMEC TO
SAY SO UNDER OATH.
NCMEC asks the Court to dismiss this action on the ground that its April 22 statements are
true. ECF No. 11 at 8-9. NCMEC holds the records that would show it. Plaintiff does not.
The letters used Plaintiff's complete legal name. Plaintiff has declared that he never used
that name on any Meta account. ECF No. 31 19 3-6. No Defendant has stated in any filing that a
report contains that name.
The Offer gives NCMEC one hour to substantiate its statements. One witness answers six
questions: whether NCMEC holds the two reports, when it received each and from whom, whether
Meta submitted either, whether either contains the name "Marvelle J. Ballentine," how that name
came to appear in any associated record, and what NCMEC reviewed before it sent the letters.
NCMEC may maintain every position it has taken. The Offer requires no particular answer.
Plaintiff asks for an account of why his name appeared in those letters. In exchange he
gives up every claim against NCMEC, Hall, and NCMEC's personnel.
IV.
PLAINTIFF HAS OFFERED TO END THIS CASE WITHOUT PAYMENT
BEFORE.
ECF No. 136 describes the cost of this litigation to NCMEC. The record shows the
following.

Plaintiff states the July 31 offer for the purpose Federal Rule of Evidence 408(b) permits.
It is offered to answer ECF No. 136's statements about resources. It is not offered to prove liability

V.
ONE HOUR OF TESTIMONY WOULD END EVERY PENDING MATTER AS
TO NCMEC AND HALL.
Dismissal of NCMEC and Hall would end, as to them, the need to decide:
the motions to dismiss filed by NCMEC and Hall (ECF Nos. 10, 45);
the motion for leave to amend (ECF No. 114);
• the renewed Rule 56 motion (ECF No. 116) and the motion to extend the time to
respond to it (ECF No. 137);
the Rule 72(a) objections (ECF Nos. 66, 89, 97) and the motions filed with them
(ECF Nos. 67, 90, 93, 98);
6

•
the motions directed to the October 22 and October 29 orders (ECF Nos. 109,
112, 118, 120, 122);
•
the motions for leave to file and the request for judicial notice (ECF Nos. 76, 124,
126, 128); and
•
ECF No. 133.
Meta's motion to dismiss (ECF No. 21) and Plaintiff's claims against Meta would remain.
NCMEC would bear the cost of preparing one witness to answer six questions about two
letters and two reports. Plaintiff would bear the cost of the recording. No other cost follows.
The Court is not asked to require any Defendant to accept. The Court is asked to consider
that one hour of testimony would remove NCMEC and Hall from each matter listed above.
VI. WHAT THE COURT IS ASKED TO DO
Plaintiff asks the Court to grant leave, to deem Exhibit A filed, and to consider it in ruling
on ECF No. 133. Plaintiff does not ask the Court to direct any Defendant to accept, reject, or
respond to the Offer.
CONCLUSION
The Motion should be granted.
